_comment: 🎚️ The config state lane of `s.trinity.jack`'s editor (✏️editor/🎭️modes/✏️edit/🪟️windows/📝️editor/🎚️config): its mutation vocabulary `JackEditorWindowConfigMutation` over `JackEditorWindowConfig`, measured by the plugin bridge on the surface coordinate, claimed by `../../🧪️tests/🎚️mutate-trinity-jack-1-any-editor-edit-editor-config` and backed by one committed vector per declared outcome class.

noOracleDecisions.rationale: `JackEditorWindowConfigMutation` is the config state lane of `s.trinity.jack`'s ✏️editor/🎭️modes/✏️edit/🪟️windows/📝️editor/🎚️config surface: it holds one query editor window's jack query text. This is this repository's own editor state record, not a published format, so no third party implements it. What is under test is that each kind (`set-query`) changes exactly its own part of `JackEditorWindowConfig`, and that every kind's computed inverse, read off the pre-mutation record, restores it exactly. Confidence comes from one committed, handcrafted (before, mutation, after, diff, outcome) vector per kind and declared outcome class under `../🧫️fixtures/`, exercised end to end through the production dispatch bridge, and from the inverse law as a metamorphic property.

candidatesConsidered.reason: A persisted key-value store for desktop settings; it has no model of this surface's typed state record, its per-kind setters or the inverse each kind computes.
Loads and stores a whole configuration struct on disk; it defines no typed state mutations and neither their no-op nor their inverse behaviour.

referenceSurvey.whyNoneQualifies: `JackEditorWindowConfig` is a state record defined by this repository with its own typed mutation vocabulary; generic state containers can hold its values but cannot adjudicate what each kind must change or what its inverse is.

provenance.attribution: Handcrafted before/mutation/after vector authored against this state lane's own schema; the diff and diagnostics are the production dispatch's, reviewed against the after-snapshot.

fixtureManifests.notes: Typing a new query replaces the editor window's query text.
